conviction: Moderate; a competition investment judgment, not an estimated winning probability
selection_chronology: All scenario prices were known before this selection. This is an explicit reconsideration after external market and expectations research, not a blinded forecast choice or a newly discovered numerical result.
why_this_operating_case: The independent TrendForce shipment forecast permits Intel unit growth despite loss of share. A 40% industry growth scenario with rounded 50% to 42% Intel shipment shares gives 17.6% Intel unit growth. The stronger case needs about 21.9% annual ASP growth on its own 2026 estimate, less than the latest reported year-on-year increase but still an assumption about mix and prices.
Current Xeon deployments and multigeneration customer relationships support continued adoption. They do not establish contract economics or guarantee share.
Pooled Q2/Q3 conditional CPU margin is a reasonable forward anchor during a product transition. The full-YTD anchor is a useful adverse alternative, not inherently the best forecast.

After rapid expansion, the inherited gradual CPU growth fade permits about 6.04% annual revenue growth in 2031-40. Its direction is consistent with continued workload adoption and a maturing market; its exact rates remain owned assumptions.
The forecast disagreement is specific: 2028 consolidated sales about90.015B versus a public S&P Global series of83.719B. No matched CPU-share consensus has been located.
why_this_risk_method: The pre-existing trailing-cash implied equity premium uses observed market distributions without imposing the sustainable-payout model's mature payout uplift. This is a methodological preference, not evidence of reduced Intel business risk. Hold 4.94% Treasury and1.5 asset beta fixed. The11.555% sustainable-payout result remains on the valuation page and can reverse the planning-value premium.
required_disclosures: The adopted case was previously labeled favorable. Promotion to an owned central thesis does not make its joint assumptions observed or statistically most likely.

No new high-volume external wafer-customer breakthrough is required, but existing external revenue and a7B gross packaging forecast remain included. Do not imply zero external business.
Shortage relief, package yields, mature margins, foundry recovery and growth capital productivity remain forecasts. No completed original interview or proprietary shipment data is claimed.
A low-return long scenario is not sufficient evidence for a profitable outright short.
three_claims: Intel can grow CPU sales while losing shipment share.
New Xeon adoption can support richer mix beyond the immediate shortage, with measurable competition and cost risks.
The return comes from factory and cash-flow recovery; a large external wafer win is additional upside rather than the core requirement.
